title: Capital and Liquidity Basics
summary: The purpose of capital and liquidity requirements, how they are measured and how supervisors judge whether a firm holds enough to absorb losses and meet obligations.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The purpose of capital and liquidity requirements, how they are measured and how supervisors judge whether a firm holds enough to absorb losses and meet obligations.
Learning Objectives: Explain the purpose of capital and liquidity in protecting customers and markets
Describe how capital requirements and liquidity measures are calculated in outline
Assess whether a firm's capital and liquidity position supports its business plan
Syllabus: Loss absorption, quality of capital and own funds
Risk-weighted assets, leverage and fixed overheads requirements in outline
Liquidity risk, funding profiles, buffers and stress
Reading regulatory returns and capital planning
Intended Audience: New joiners and developing staff in supervisory, authorisation and policy functions
Supervisors and inspectors moving into a new sector or wishing to strengthen their financial analysis
Staff from legal, enforcement or support functions who need to understand firms' business and finances
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No accounting qualification is required. Basic numeracy and some familiarity with financial services are helpful.
Core Reading: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (2024), Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (2008), Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision
IOSCO (2017), Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation
FSB (2023), High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-asset Activities and Markets
